situation.summary: Post-tenancy sanitation, waste removal and rear garden clearance at 18 Thistlevaunt Lane (vacant) has been on hold since 10 Sep. The contractor's £665 quote (A2) was approved by the landlord only "if recovered from the bond" (E008, E010), but the contractor was told it was approved without that condition (E009). The agency is also pursuing a deposit claim, and the landlord's 17 Sep "approved quote" (E016) is unidentified. A prospective tenant is due to move in on 28 Sep (E015), and the 25 Sep instruction to wait three more working days (E021) runs past that date. No visit is booked, and the separate major maintenance that the hold depends on has no recorded approval or completion.

decision.message:
HOLD: 18 Thistlevaunt Lane, post-tenancy sanitation, waste removal and garden clearance (Brindlewick quote NBL-015-Q1, £665).
Reason: Mira Venn told us on 25 Sep to wait three more working days. The separate major maintenance has to be finished before this work can be booked (E021). No visit is booked and nothing records the maintenance as finished. Keep Brindlewick on hold, as they were told on 10 and 16 Sep (E012, E015).
Recheck on Tue 30 Sep 2025:
1. Has the separate major maintenance been finished, or at least scheduled? If not, ask Mira Venn and Tovan Rusk for its status and expected finish date.
2. Before anyone instructs Brindlewick, sort out the approval:
   (a) Nessa Quill approved the £665 only if it is recovered from the bond (E008, E010).
   (b) She never answered whether the work can go ahead while the deposit claim is pending (E011).
   (c) Her 17 Sep "approved quote" (E016) does not say which quote it means. It could be the separate maintenance quote (E015).
   Ask her to confirm in writing which quote she approved, and whether the £665 work may go ahead now, whatever the deposit outcome.
3. Correct what Brindlewick was told. On 8 Sep they heard the quote was approved, with no mention of the bond condition (E009). Then put the scope gap to the landlord: the quote does not mention making good the soil disturbed by digging (A1). Also confirm the VAT basis of the £665 with Brindlewick (A2 has no VAT line).
4. Get Brindlewick's possible dates in writing. They said on the 21 Sep call that they would send them (E019). Nothing in writing is recorded.
5. Raise with Mira Venn that the prospective tenant's 28 Sep move-in (E015) falls before this hold ends.
If the deposit-recovery condition becomes a dispute, or the landlord will not approve unless recovery is guaranteed, hand it to a person to decide. Do not book or instruct the contractor until 1–3 are resolved.
decision.rationale: The latest real event is the property manager's own instruction (E021): wait three more working days because the separate major maintenance must be finished before this work can be booked. That is a hold by someone with authority, with a time limit that has not passed, and nothing urgent or unsafe is on record. The checklist rule for a "promised date or condition not yet passed" therefore points to waiting. Escalating would hand the case back to the person who made this decision this morning. The deposit claim is already being prepared by the property manager (E011). The open questions (the conditional approval, the unclear "approved quote", the condition missing from the 8 Sep contractor message, the soil scope) block booking, but booking cannot happen until the maintenance is done anyway. They are listed for the recheck so they are dealt with before any instruction goes out. The colleague's draft proposes escalating, but that would duplicate a decision a person has just made. Escalation is kept as the route if the bond condition turns into a dispute.
decision.expectedOutcome: Nothing goes out now. On 30 Sep we check the separate maintenance, then clear up the landlord's approval before Brindlewick is given a date.
